The left-side network has an impedance connected in series on the upper wire, labeled Z1 = 10∠30° Ω; the lower wire is directly connected through, so the left-side part is a series impedance network. In the right-side network there is a vertical element connected from the upper wire to the lower wire, labeled Z2, so the right-side part is a parallel/shunt branch impedance network. Reasoning: According to the specified method, the ABCD matrix of the left-side series impedance network is M1 = [[1, Z1], [0, 1]]. The admittance of the right-side parallel impedance Z2 is 1/Z2, and its ABCD matrix is M2 = [[1, 0], [1/Z2, 1]]. The total cascade matrix M = M1 M2 = [[1, Z1], [0, 1]] [[1, 0], [1/Z2, 1]]. After multiplication, the C element of the matrix is 1/Z2. The problem gives C = 0.025∠45°, so 1/Z2 = 0.025∠45°. Therefore Z2 = 1/C = 1/(0.025∠45°) = 40∠-45° Ω.
